blogs.title: D.C. Circuit Doubles Down on Exemption 7(A) Deference in National-Security Files
blogs.description: This post analyzes how Farahi reinforces the D.C. Circuit’s long-standing deference to the FBI when Exemption 7(A) intersects with national security. It explores the court’s reliance on CREW, Juarez, and CNSS to accept agency attestations that proceedings are ongoing, the low evidentiary threshold for demonstrating interference with enforcement, and the court’s willingness to consider the breadth of the underlying counterterrorism investigation. It also considers what this means for FOIA requesters seeking to challenge 7(A) with staleness arguments and whether Farahi signals an increasingly durable shield for terrorism-related files.

blogs.title: ‘Stale’ No More: Managing Time in FOIA Through Updated Declarations
blogs.description: Focusing on procedure, this post examines the court’s treatment of potentially stale agency declarations and its acceptance of the Bender ‘update’ as a bridge to earlier, more detailed Hardy declarations. It unpacks the district court’s insistence on refreshed showings after years of litigation, the appellate court’s approval of using a terse update to confirm continuing proceedings, and the practical playbook this creates for agencies and requesters: when courts will demand updates, how much detail is needed, and how to preserve challenges to timeliness and sufficiency.

blogs.title: Ex Parte and Inextricably Intertwined: Segregability in the Shadow of National Security
blogs.description: This post explores the court’s segregability analysis and heavy reliance on ex parte submissions. It explains why the panel accepted the FBI’s claim that non-exempt material was not reasonably segregable because it was interspersed and lacked meaningful information content, and how precedents like Mead and Perioperative Services frame that inquiry. It also considers due-process tensions posed by ex parte practice in FOIA and offers strategic guidance for plaintiffs seeking to contest segregability without access to the sealed record.

blogs.title: Category Definitions, Forfeiture, and the Vaughn Playbook After Farahi
blogs.description: This post addresses the underdeveloped but important issue of categorical withholdings. It analyzes the court’s brief discussion of category sufficiency under CREW and Gallant, why Farahi’s failure to specifically contest category scope led to forfeiture, and what a properly preserved challenge should look like. The piece offers practical guidance on building record-specific objections to overbroad categories and forecasting how agencies might structure future Vaughn submissions to withstand D.C. Circuit scrutiny.
